seo.title: Help for people experiencing homelessness in Toronto - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help in Toronto for people experiencing homelessness: shelter access, food, drop-ins, health care, benefits, jobs, documents and legal help.

page.heading: Toronto — help for people experiencing homelessness

notice.text: Hours, eligibility and available spaces can change.
Call before travelling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, payment, appointment, document or job. During severe weather, check the City page or call 311 for activated sites.

content.text: When asking for help, say where you are, your age, any urgent health or accessibility needs, whether children or a pet are with you, and whether you have a safe place tonight. Central Intake is the main route into the City shelter system; most shelter addresses are not direct walk-in access.
No Home Help is not part of the City or any service provider. Verify information before travelling.
Phone:
. Call for immediate danger, a serious medical emergency, fire or a crime in progress.
Give the exact location or nearest intersection, what is happening and how many people need help. If it is safe, stay on the line and follow the operator's instructions.
Make the right call — City of Toronto

items.name: Central Intake — shelter and respite access

content.text: Toronto:
Toll-free:
. Available 24 hours, every day; you can also call 311.

Central Intake matches people with available emergency shelter or 24-hour respite spaces. Say if you are a family, youth, woman, Indigenous person, couple, have accessibility needs or have a pet. A call does not guarantee an immediate space; ask what to do if nothing is available and keep the callback number active if you can.
Central Intake — City of Toronto
Inside Toronto:
Outside the city:
TTY:
711. Available 24 hours.

Ask for street outreach, an activated warming centre, City services or help reaching Central Intake. For a person outside, give a precise location, description and any immediate risks. 311 is not emergency dispatch.
311 Toronto — City of Toronto
Call:
, 24 hours, in many languages. The service is free and confidential.
Ask for nearby food, clothing, housing help, health services, financial assistance or a crisis team. The navigator can explain eligibility and access, but cannot promise a place or service.
211 Ontario
Request outreach:
call
. Outreach teams engage people sleeping outside and can work on shelter, identification, income and housing options.
Give the nearest address or intersection and describe the person's location. Outreach is voluntary and response is based on urgency and team availability; call 911 for an immediate threat to life.
Homeless Help — City of Toronto
Outreach or City information:
Questions about belongings stored after an encampment move:

City outreach staff offer shelter and housing connections before and during encampment responses. Ask staff for written information about storage, retrieval deadlines and where items are taken. For immediate danger, call 911.
Encampment outreach response — City of Toronto
Phone:
. Use it for a non-urgent police matter. For danger or a crime in progress, call 911.
If the problem is primarily homelessness, welfare or mental health and no one is in immediate danger, 311, 211 or the Toronto Community Crisis Service may be more appropriate.
Police non-emergency — Toronto Police Service
Toronto shelters operate 24 hours and may provide meals, laundry, case management, health or harm-reduction support. Sites serve different groups and some addresses are confidential.
Access:
call Central Intake at
or
. Do not travel to a listed shelter expecting admission unless Central Intake or the shelter tells you to go.
Shelters — City of Toronto
Respite sites provide an indoor place to rest, meals and referrals. Toronto states that its 24-hour respite sites are pet-friendly; capacity and rules still vary.
Access:
Central Intake,
. Seasonal winter respite sites may accept walk-ins from November 15 to April 15; confirm the current site and access route before travelling.
24-hour respite sites — City of Toronto
Warming centres are temporary, walk-in sites activated during cold weather. They offer a warm indoor space, washrooms and meals, and are pet-friendly. Central Intake referral is not required.
Before travelling:
call
or check the City page to confirm that centres are activated and which addresses are open. Activation can change with the forecast.
Toronto warming centres — City of Toronto
The City's current list includes 81 Elizabeth Street, 349 George Street, 885 Scarborough Golf Club Road, 12 Holmes Avenue and 136 Spadina Road. Accessibility and showers differ by site.
These sites only operate when activated. Confirm through 311 immediately before going; do not rely on this list during a different winter season.
Current locations and accessibility — City of Toronto

Bed access:

Faith-based shelter and community service for men.

call Central Intake. The daytime drop-in and meal program has separate direct-service hours.
Good Shepherd Ministries
Low-barrier, women-only service operating 24 hours, with food, hygiene, laundry, clothing, case management and harm-reduction support. It is a drop-in, not a guaranteed shelter bed.
Check the current location and any temporary service notice on the provider's page before travelling, or ask 211.
Drop-ins and community programs — Fred Victor
Toronto's directory lists free drop-ins with meals and combinations of showers, laundry, clothing, harm-reduction supplies, housing help and other services.
Hours and programs change. Use the filters, then call the listed provider before making a long trip. A meal or service can run out before closing time.
Drop-ins — City of Toronto

items.name: Daily Bread — find a food bank

content.text: Search by address for a nearby food bank and see its current appointment, drop-in and closure information. If online registration is difficult, call
Requirements vary by location. Check the individual program before going and bring identification only if the listing says it is needed.
Find a food bank — Daily Bread
Address:
191 New Toronto Street, Gate 1
The Daily Bread site offers food-bank access and information and referral services. Some periods are drop-in and others require an appointment; closures can change.
Before going:
use the current listing or call
New Toronto Street Food Bank — Daily Bread
Address:
502 Spadina Avenue
Phone:
. The faith-based centre publishes weekday breakfast and lunch, showers, laundry, clothing and food-bank services.
Service blocks and meal times differ by day. Check the current Toronto Drop-In Network listing or call before going; practical assistance is subject to daily capacity.
Scott Mission service listing — Toronto Drop-In Network

items.name: Good Shepherd community meal and drop-in

content.text: Address:
412 Queen Street East
Phone:
. The faith-based drop-in offers meals and may provide showers, laundry, storage, a food bank and help for veterans.
The City directory currently lists a daily afternoon drop-in. Call before going because the schedule and capacity may change.
Community meals — Good Shepherd Ministries
Faith-based community offering meals, basic medical care, showers, personal-care items, clothing, computers, phones, Wi-Fi and pastoral care.
Check the current community schedule and location before going. Services are offered in a community setting and are subject to staffing and supplies.
What we do — Sanctuary Toronto

content.text: Address:
162 Bloor Street West
Phone:
. The Anglican church's weekday drop-in publishes breakfast and lunch, toiletries, basic health care, housing referrals and outdoor meal service.
Current times differ between indoor and outdoor service. Confirm on the church page before travelling.
The Common Table — Church of the Redeemer
Address:
40 Oak Street
Phone:
. The City directory lists weekday meals, showers, laundry and harm-reduction support. The site is accessible and pet-friendly.
Wednesday hours differ from other weekdays. Check the current City listing before going.
Current drop-in details — City of Toronto

content.text: Address:
170 Jarvis Street
Phone:
. Offers meals, showers, laundry, lockers and harm-reduction support for older men. The City lists the site as accessible and pet-friendly.
Weekend and weekday hours differ. Call or use the City directory before travelling.
Current drop-in details — City of Toronto
Address:
729 St. Clair Avenue West
Phone:
. The City directory lists weekday meals, a food bank and harm-reduction support.
Programs may have different registration and service times. Call first or check the current directory.
Current drop-in details — City of Toronto

. Faith-based drop-in listed by the City with community meals on selected days.
Meal times are not identical every day. Check the current City directory or call before going.

. Offers meals, showers, laundry and harm-reduction services on listed weekday mornings and Sundays.
Call first because service hours and availability can change.
Current drop-in details — City of Toronto

850–854 Bloor Street West
Phone:
. The weekday drop-in offers meals, showers, laundry, a food bank and harm-reduction support; the City lists it as accessible and pet-friendly.
Confirm hours before going, especially around holidays.
Current drop-in details — City of Toronto
Address:
365 Spadina Avenue
Phone:
. For youth aged 16 to 24, with meals, showers, laundry, clothing, identification and other support.
The published schedule is weekday afternoons and closes earlier on Friday. Confirm before going.
Youth drop-in — Yonge Street Mission

Use the City drop-in directory and select services such as showers, laundry or clothing. Fred Victor 40 Oak, Haven Toronto, Good Shepherd, The Corner and Christie Ossington are among the current listings.
Call first. Machines, towels, clothing sizes and the number of service slots are limited and may run out.
Drop-ins and services — City of Toronto
The City map shows public washrooms, portable toilets and drinking-water locations, with opening dates, hours and accessibility where available.
Facilities can close for maintenance or winter. Check the entry before walking there; call 311 if the information appears wrong.
Washrooms and drinking-water map — City of Toronto

items.name: Toronto Public Library — internet and computers

content.text: All Toronto Public Library branches offer free Wi-Fi. Library computers can normally be booked for up to 120 minutes per day, subject to availability.
If you do not have a library card, ask staff about a computer guest pass. Branch hours and computer availability differ.
Computer services — Toronto Public Library
Toronto Public Library states that Access cards are intended for people without a permanent address and are renewed annually.
Ask at a branch what identification or proof is accepted. An Access card may have different borrowing conditions from a standard card.
Library card information — Toronto Public Library
The City publishes free Wi-Fi locations at selected civic and community sites. The map includes the network name and address.
Public Wi-Fi is not private. Avoid sending banking, identity or benefit passwords unless the website is secure and you can log out fully.
ConnectTO locations — City of Toronto
Scott Mission, Sanctuary Toronto, Friends of Ruby and several City-listed drop-ins provide clothing or hygiene supplies when available.
Call before going and say the item and size needed. Donations vary daily; no site can guarantee stock.
Search drop-in services — City of Toronto

categories.title: 5. Health, mental health and substance use

content.text: Phone:
, free and confidential, 24 hours. A registered nurse can help decide whether to use emergency care, a clinic or self-care.
Health811 is not an ambulance and cannot diagnose every problem. Call 911 for chest pain, severe breathing trouble, unconsciousness, major bleeding, overdose or another immediate threat to life.
Health811 Ontario
Access:
call
, 24 hours. Free, city-wide, non-police mobile crisis support for people aged 16 and older.
Use it for a mental-health crisis when no one is in immediate danger. The 211 navigator assesses the call and may dispatch a community crisis team; response depends on safety and availability.
Toronto Community Crisis Service — City of Toronto
Call or text:
, 24 hours. Use it if you are thinking about suicide or worried about someone else.
For an attempt in progress, immediate physical danger or a medical emergency, call 911. You can contact 988 even if you are not sure how serious the situation is.
988 Canada
24-hour crisis line:
. Offers telephone support, mobile crisis intervention and short-term crisis beds for eligible adults.
A bed or in-person response is not guaranteed. Call 911 for immediate danger or a life-threatening medical emergency.
Gerstein Crisis Centre

items.name: ConnexOntario — mental health, gambling and substance use

content.text: Phone:
Text:
CONNEX to 247247. Free, confidential information and referral, 24 hours.
A navigator can identify treatment, withdrawal-management and community options. It does not guarantee immediate admission; call 911 for a medical emergency or suspected overdose.
ConnexOntario
Address:
1051 Queen Street West
Open 24 hours for adults aged 16 and older experiencing a psychiatric emergency; no referral is required. Patients are triaged, so waiting time varies.
Call 911 if travel is unsafe or there is immediate danger. This emergency department is not a general shelter or drop-in.
Psychiatric Emergency Department — CAMH
Address:
338 Dundas Street East
Phone:
. Provides low-barrier health and social services. Current published opening days are Monday to Friday, with a later Tuesday start; nursing drop-in is offered on selected days.
Programs have separate hours and may reach capacity. Check the current-hours page before going.
Current hours — Street Health
Address:
338 Dundas Street East
Provides a supervised space and harm-reduction support. Hours can differ from the main Street Health schedule.
For a suspected overdose, call 911, give naloxone if available and follow emergency instructions. Do not wait for a site to open.
Overdose-prevention site — Street Health

items.name: Free dental care for eligible residents

content.text: Toronto Public Health:
. The City operates dental clinics for eligible Toronto residents who do not have dental insurance and cannot afford treatment.
Eligibility, clinic location and available treatment must be confirmed before going. Emergency dental care may still require an assessment or appointment.
Dental and oral health services — City of Toronto
Phone:
. For eligible low-income Toronto residents who are not receiving Ontario Works, Emergency Assistance or ODSP, the fund may help with approved health items such as dental care or eyeglasses.
Apply and obtain approval before paying. Eligibility and covered costs are assessed; reimbursement or approval is not guaranteed.
Health support and Hardship Fund — City of Toronto
Apply by phone:
, Monday to Friday during business hours; online applications are available at any time.

Ontario Works may provide income and employment support if eligible. Emergency Assistance may apply in an urgent crisis such as having no shelter, food or essential medication. If you have no fixed address, Toronto says you may use the nearest Employment and Social Services office address. Approval is not automatic.
Ontario Works — City of Toronto
Application support:
. ODSP provides income and employment support to eligible people with disabilities.
The application requires medical and financial information and can take time. Ask Ontario Works or a community legal clinic about interim help if you have no income while waiting.
ODSP — Government of Ontario

items.name: Toronto Employment and Social Services offices

content.text: Use the City list to find the office serving your postal code or nearest location. Offices can help with Ontario Works, documents, employment services and referrals.
Check whether an appointment is required and what to bring. If you have no address, explain this when contacting the office.
Office locations — City of Toronto
Eligible Ontario Works or ODSP recipients may receive help for approved housing costs such as moving, rent, energy arrears or establishing a home.
Before paying:
contact your caseworker. Funding is based on rules, documents and maximum amounts; it is not guaranteed.
Housing Stabilization Fund — City of Toronto
Phone:
, weekdays during published business hours. The program offers grants for eligible low-income tenants facing rent arrears or needing a rental deposit.
Call before an eviction date if possible. Income, tenancy and other conditions apply; the Rent Bank cannot guarantee payment or stop an eviction by itself.
Toronto Rent Bank — City of Toronto
Housing Help Centre:
. Toronto's map lists housing-help agencies, eviction prevention, legal help and services for specific groups.
Agencies can help with searches, applications and landlord issues, but cannot guarantee an affordable unit. Ask which office covers your area and whether an appointment is needed.
Housing help and support services — City of Toronto
People cannot apply directly to Coordinated Access. A participating housing or homelessness worker completes an assessment and may connect an eligible person to supportive housing opportunities.
General housing help:
Indigenous housing support:
. Assessment does not guarantee housing or set a move-in date.
Coordinated Access — City of Toronto
Eligible Toronto residents aged 20 to 64 can receive a discount on adult TTC fares loaded to a PRESTO card. Income and residency conditions apply.
Use the City eligibility checker or ask a social-services worker. The discount is not immediate until the application is approved and linked to the card.
Fair Pass Transit Discount — City of Toronto

items.name: Toronto Employment and Social Services — employment centres

content.text: City employment centres provide free access to job-search support and equipment such as computers and printers. Services are available to Toronto residents, not only Ontario Works recipients.
Ask about an intake appointment, résumé help, training referrals and interview preparation. A referral does not guarantee training funding or a job.
Employment services — City of Toronto
Toronto:
Toll-free:
. Employment Ontario offers free job-search, résumé, interview, training and career-planning support.
Ask for the nearest service provider and whether an appointment is required. Training and financial supports have separate eligibility rules.
Employment Ontario offices — Government of Ontario
Phone:
. Free employment help may include job planning, training and assistance with some interview or work-start costs when eligible.
Ask what program fits your situation and what documents are needed. Transit, clothing, equipment, certificates or phone help are assessed and not guaranteed.
Employment and training — Fred Victor
Adults:
270 Gerrard Street East.
Youth:
365 Spadina Avenue.
Main phone:
; ask for adult extension 4275 or youth extension 2278. Services include one-to-one employment planning and job-search support.
The program requires legal entitlement to work in Canada and may request original identification and a Social Insurance Number. Call before going.
Employment support — Yonge Street Mission
Government job-search service with listings, job-market information and résumé tools. Search by Toronto and filter for language, schedule and employment type.
Never pay a recruiter to release wages or send banking passwords by email. Confirm the employer independently before sharing identity documents.
Job Bank — Government of Canada
Address:
338 Dundas Street East

Street Health can help eligible clients replace or obtain documents including birth certificates, health cards and some status documents. It does not process passports, driver's licences, permanent-resident cards or citizenship cards.
ID clinic hours are limited and can reach capacity. Check the current schedule before going and bring any document or photocopy you still have.
Identification services — Street Health

items.name: ID Safe — document storage and mailing address

content.text: Street Health's ID Safe offers secure storage for identification and may provide a mailing address for people who are homeless or vulnerably housed.
Ask how mail pickup, authorization and replacement work before leaving originals. Capacity and eligibility apply.
ID Safe — Street Health
Service Canada:
. Apply online, by mail or in person for a SIN if eligible; Canada no longer issues plastic SIN cards.
Use only the official Government of Canada service. Do not carry a written SIN unless necessary and do not give it to a landlord or food bank.
Apply for a SIN — Government of Canada

items.name: Taxes and benefits without stable housing

content.text: You can file a tax return even with no income and may use a shelter or temporary address where you can safely receive mail. Filing may unlock benefits and credits.
Free volunteer tax clinics assist eligible people with simple returns. Check the clinic's appointment, income and document rules.
Tax information for people experiencing housing insecurity — Canada Revenue Agency
Find a free tax clinic — Canada Revenue Agency
Toronto:
Toll-free:
. Weekday telephone help is available in many languages.
Legal Aid can explain services and financial eligibility for criminal, family, immigration and some other legal matters. Calling does not guarantee a certificate or lawyer.
Contact Legal Aid Ontario
Address:
655 Spadina Avenue
Phone:
. Community legal clinic operated with the University of Toronto, providing free help in selected areas to eligible clients.
Call before going. The clinic cannot accept every case and may refer you elsewhere.
Downtown Legal Services
Address:
163 Queen Street East, Unit 101
Phone:
. Helps eligible residents with matters including housing, income security, immigration and employment.
Service is generally by appointment and catchment or eligibility rules apply. Call first.
Neighbourhood Legal Services — Legal Aid Ontario
Phone:
. Free legal information and limited assistance for eligible tenants dealing with a Landlord and Tenant Board matter.
Contact the program as early as possible and keep every notice, lease, rent receipt and hearing document. Assistance does not guarantee representation or a result.
Tenant Duty Counsel — Advocacy Centre for Tenants Ontario

items.name: If you receive an eviction notice

content.text: An eviction notice does not by itself mean that you must leave immediately. Only the Landlord and Tenant Board can issue an eviction order, and enforcement follows a legal process.
Do not ignore deadlines. Contact a community legal clinic, Tenant Duty Counsel or a housing-help centre and keep a copy or photo of every notice.
Understand and prevent evictions — City of Toronto
Address:
208 Oakwood Avenue
Phone:
WhatsApp:
. Provides information and support to refugees, claimants and people with uncertain immigration status.
The centre publishes a Monday first-visit walk-in process, except holidays. Waiting is possible; check current instructions before going.
Contact FCJ Refugee Centre

items.name: Legal Aid Ontario Refugee Law Office

content.text: Address:
20 Dundas Street West, Suite 730
Phone:
. Provides legal services in refugee and immigration matters subject to mandate and eligibility.
Call before going and say if there is a hearing, removal date or filing deadline. Bring all immigration documents, even if expired.
Legal Aid Ontario locations and contact

categories.title: 10. Women, youth, 2SLGBTQIA+, Indigenous people, veterans and pets

content.text: GTA:
Toll-free:
Selected mobile phones:
#SAFE (#7233). Available 24 hours in more than 200 languages.
Anonymous, confidential safety planning and referral to shelters. Shelter addresses are confidential and space is not guaranteed. In immediate danger call 911.
Services — Assaulted Women's Helpline

items.name: Toronto Rape Crisis Centre / Multicultural Women Against Rape

content.text: 24-hour crisis line:
. Anonymous and confidential support after sexual violence.
The line offers emotional support and information, not emergency dispatch. If you are in immediate danger or need urgent medical care, call 911.
Crisis line — TRCC/MWAR
Call:
Text:
CONNECT to 686868. Free, confidential support for young people, 24 hours.
Use 911 for immediate danger. For a youth shelter bed in Toronto, call Central Intake and state the young person's age.
Urgent help — Kids Help Phone
Drop-in:
70 Richmond Street East, Suite 400
Phone:
. Free drop-in for 2SLGBTQIA+ youth aged 16 to 29, with groceries, Wi-Fi, computers, clothing, laundry, hygiene and harm-reduction supplies, case management and mental-health support.
Weekday hours differ by day. Check the current weekly schedule. Transitional housing has a separate application, eligibility rules and no guaranteed vacancy.
Programs and services — Friends of Ruby
Address:
519 Church Street
Phone:
. Offers programs and selected drop-ins for 2SLGBTQ+ communities, including meals, food access and referrals. The City lists relevant drop-ins as pet-friendly.
Programs serve different groups and run on different days. Check the current schedule before going.
Programs — The 519
Address:
333 Sherbourne Street, second floor
Phone:
. Services for 2SLGBTQ youth may include meals, showers, a food bank and harm-reduction support.
Drop-in days and hours vary. Confirm through the City drop-in directory or Sherbourne Health before travelling.
Current drop-in details — City of Toronto

items.name: Native Women's Resource Centre of Toronto

content.text: Address:
191 Gerrard Street East
Phone:
. Indigenous-led support for women and families, including drop-in, housing, family, trauma and practical programs.
Published weekday hours include a midday closure. Call before going and ask which program is available that day.
Program directory — Native Women's Resource Centre of Toronto
Aboriginal Housing Support Centre:
. Ask for Indigenous-specific housing navigation and connection to Coordinated Access.
An assessment or referral does not guarantee housing. For an emergency shelter bed, still call Central Intake and identify yourself as Indigenous if you are comfortable doing so.
Indigenous access information — City of Toronto
Veterans Affairs Canada:
. Staff can connect an eligible veteran or family member with case management, benefits and community services.
Good Shepherd's drop-in also lists veterans navigation. Say that you served when contacting Central Intake or a drop-in so staff can identify specialist support.
Veteran homelessness support — Veterans Affairs Canada
Eligible veterans and certain family members facing a financial emergency may apply for help with essentials such as food, clothing, uninsured health costs or shelter.
Apply or ask for help:
. The program verifies service, identity, residence and need; payment is assessed case by case and is not guaranteed.
Veterans Emergency Fund — Veterans Affairs Canada

Tell Central Intake about the animal before accepting a referral. Toronto states that 24-hour respite sites and activated warming centres are pet-friendly, but not every shelter can accommodate every animal.
Ask what supplies or documentation are needed and whether the pet can stay with you. Do not abandon or hide an animal to enter a site.
Pet services in homeless shelters — City of Toronto
For clients of participating shelters and 24-hour homelessness services, HelpingPawsTO may provide free veterinary care such as an exam, vaccination, spay or neuter, microchip and parasite treatment.
Access is by staff referral
, not direct walk-in. Supplies and appointments depend on availability. Ask your shelter or service worker.
HelpingPawsTO — City of Toronto

This page prioritizes current government pages and the providers' own websites. Toronto's directories can change without notice; confirm before travelling and report a broken link or incorrect detail.
